title: Creating and Using a Class
objective: Define a class, initialize it with a constructor, and call a method on an instance you create from it.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A class is a blueprint for creating objects that bundle data and behavior together. Once you define a class, you can create as many independent instances from it as you need with the new keyword, and each instance keeps its own copy of the data described by the blueprint.

Every class that stores data on its instances defines a constructor method. JavaScript calls it automatically whenever you write new ClassName(...), so it's the natural place to set up whatever information that instance needs to start with, using this.property = value.

Inside a class, this refers to the specific instance a method is being called on. JavaScript supplies it automatically based on which instance you called the method through — you never pass it in yourself.
explanation.rule: Define a class with class ClassName { constructor(args) { this.prop = args; } }, then create an instance with new ClassName(...) and call its methods with dot notation.

checks.question: When does a class's constructor method run?
options: Every time any method on the class is called.
Automatically, once, when you write new ClassName(...).
Only if you call it by name yourself.

feedback.correct: Correct — new ClassName(...) automatically calls the constructor exactly once, to set up that new instance.
feedback.incorrect: The constructor runs automatically and exactly once, triggered by new ClassName(...) — you never call it directly.

assignment.title: Forge Badge
assignment.brief: Write a Badge class whose constructor takes a rank and stores it, with a method describe() that returns 'Rank: <rank>'.
requirements: Define class Badge with a constructor that takes rank and stores it as this.rank.
Define a describe() method that returns 'Rank: <rank>'.
Create a Badge instance and call describe() on it.

hints: The constructor's parameter and the property name can both be called rank — this.rank = rank; stores it.
this inside describe() refers to whichever Badge instance describe() was called on.
new Badge('Gold').describe() should return exactly 'Rank: Gold'.
